newsitem.title: USA: NFA expels American Futures Group, executives.
newsitem.headline: NFA expels American Futures Group, executives.

text.p: The National Futures Association (NFA) said it has expelled American Futures Group Inc (AFG), a futures commission merchant based in New York, from NFA membership.

NFA added that it also permanently barred George Perk Jr, AFG chairman and chief executive officer, and AFG president Thomas Reeves from association with and from acting as principal of any NFA member.
Former AFG vice-president Evan Tucker was also suspended from association with and acting as principal of any NFA member for two years, it said.
NFA, the self-regulatory body of the U.S. futures industry, said AFG, Perk, Reeves and Tucker may appeal the case to the NFA appeals committee.
NFA said AFG had failed to maintain adequate books and financial records and that it had used deceptive and misleading sales practices at its Seattle branch office.

NFA added that it found AFG, Perk, Reeves and Tucker engaged in conduct inconsistent with just and equitable principles of trade. It said that under Perk and Reeve's direction, Tucker trained associates of an introducing broker to employ high-pressure sales tactics and use deceptive and misleading sales solicitations.
In addition, NFA found that AFG, Perk and Reeves violated an earlier settlement agreement with NFA and failed to diligently supervise AFG's employees and agents.
